headline: Polymarket reportedly paid creators to post fake betting videos
summary: Investigation reveals the prediction market company allegedly paid creators to use dummy sites and fake winning bets in promotional videos.
details: The Wall Street Journal investigated 1,105 videos and creator guidance related to Polymarket. Their review found that 778 videos appeared to show someone placing a bet on the platform.
However, a closer examination reportedly revealed that none of these videos actually featured the real Polymarket website. Instead, creators used dummy sites designed to mimic the actual platform.
Furthermore, for over half of the videos that depicted winning bets, the actual outcome on Polymarket would have been a loss, according to the WSJ report.

Creators reportedly received materials from Polymarket to ensure their videos were convincing and engaging, with the company also allegedly employing a 'social-media army' to boost the virality of these posts.
This news comes as governments worldwide grapple with regulating prediction markets. Minnesota recently banned them, while Spain blocked Polymarket and Kalshi over potential gambling law violations.
caption:
Polymarket allegedly paid creators to post fake betting videos on TikTok, with many showing wins that would have been losses.

The Wall Street Journal investigated 1,105 videos and creator guidance related to Polymarket. Their review found that 778 videos appeared to show someone placing a bet on the platform.

However, a closer examination reportedly revealed that none of these videos actually featured the real Polymarket website. Instead, creators used dummy sites designed to mimic the actual platform.

Furthermore, for over half of the videos that depicted winning bets, the actual outcome on Polymarket would have been a loss, according to the WSJ report.

Creators reportedly received materials from Polymarket to ensure their videos were convincing and engaging, with the company also allegedly employing a 'social-media army' to boost the virality of these posts.

This news comes as governments worldwide grapple with regulating prediction markets. Minnesota recently banned them, while Spain blocked Polymarket and Kalshi over potential gambling law violations.
